mappings.note: Finding the material that is not malleable amounts to separating metals from non-metals, LO-2's own example. Not LO-1, which fits items that merely name the property.
Picking the good conductor differentiates materials by an electrical property, named in LO-1. Not LO-2, because no class is assigned.
Ductility named as the wire-drawing property is property naming. Duplicate of an earlier item and coded the same way.
Sonorousness as the ringing property of metals is a property definition. Not LO-2, since nothing is sorted.
Mercury as the liquid metal is identification by a physical property. Not LO-6, because no reaction is involved.
The ash of burnt magnesium giving a basic solution is the product character of a metal burning in air and dissolving in water. Not LO-1, because a reaction outcome rather than a property is asked.
Sulphur plus oxygen giving sulphur dioxide is a non-metal reaction with air, LO-6 word for word. Not LO-2, since no material is classified.
Sulphur dioxide dissolving in water to give an acid is the reaction of a non-metal oxide with water. Not LO-3, because nothing is investigated experimentally.
Sulphuric acid turning blue litmus red is the acid test that accompanies the non-metal oxide reactions in LO-6. Not LO-3, because the result is recalled rather than obtained from an investigation.
Non-metal oxides being acidic is the general product rule of the reaction-with-air outcome. Not LO-2, because the oxides are not being sorted into classes but characterised by reaction.
Storing sodium under kerosene is a practical safety measure. Not LO-6, because the reaction is the reason rather than the question.
The metal reacting vigorously with both oxygen and water is reaction behaviour, LO-6's subject. Not LO-1, reserved here for physical properties.
Reading the metal out of calcium hydroxide rests on knowing which elements are metals. Not LO-6, because no reaction is described, only a compound named.
The non-metal that catches fire in air is a reaction-with-air question. Not LO-1, because reactivity rather than a physical property is at issue.
Hydrogen from metals reacting with acids is the product of the metal-acid reaction in LO-6. Not LO-2, since nothing is classified.
The pop test identifies the hydrogen produced in metal-acid reactions. Not LO-3, because the pupil recalls the test result rather than designing an investigation.
The nuclear membrane separating nucleus from cytoplasm is a microscopic feature of the cell, which LO-8 asks pupils to describe. Not LO-1, because nothing is compared between plant and animal cells.
Nucleoplasm as the fluid inside the nucleus is another microscopic feature to describe. Not LO-9, because the item names a part rather than asking for a labelled drawing.
Tissues combining into organs is a step in the organisation flow chart LO-9 names. Not LO-8, because the level is above anything visible on a slide.
That cells differ in shape and size is differentiation of cells by structure. Not LO-8, because the item generalises rather than describing one observed feature.
Cells lacking a nuclear membrane, the prokaryotes, is a structural differentiation of cell types. Not LO-2, because two kinds are contrasted rather than a set sorted.
The nucleus as the control centre describes a cell part by its function. Not LO-5, because no process is traced, only the part named.
Plastids being found only in plants is the plant-versus-animal cell distinction LO-1 names verbatim. Not LO-8, because the item turns on the contrast rather than on the appearance.
Genes located on chromosomes describes a microscopic component of the nucleus. Not LO-1, because no two cell types are contrasted.
Similar cells forming a tissue is the first step of the organisation flow chart. Grouped with the tissues-to-organs item for the same reason.
Calling a single-celled organism unicellular classifies organisms by a characteristic. Not LO-1, because no two organisms are contrasted.
The cell wall being found in plant cells is the plant/animal cell differentiation. Not LO-8, because the answer is a comparison rather than an observed feature.
Vacuoles as the blank-looking structures in cytoplasm is exactly a microscopic feature to describe. Not LO-1, since no contrast is drawn.
Plasma membrane as the other name for cell membrane names a cell part. Not LO-9, because no diagram is required.
The cell as the basic structural and functional unit is the summary description of what a slide shows. Not LO-9, because nothing is drawn or charted.
Chromosomes located in the nucleus describes the internal features of the cell. Not LO-1, because no cell types are compared.
The longest human cell, the nerve cell, differentiates cells by structure and size. Not LO-8, because the item ranks cell types rather than describing a slide.
Placing blood among connective tissues classifies tissues by characteristic. Not LO-1, because a class is assigned rather than two things contrasted.
Matching smooth muscle to the organs that contain it applies the tissue classification. Not LO-9, since no diagram or chart is produced.
The cell wall as the non-living part of a plant cell differentiates cell structures by property. Not LO-8, because the answer rests on the living/non-living contrast.
Finding the organelle without DNA differentiates organelles by a structural property. Not LO-8, because the pupil must compare organelles rather than describe one.

The difference between cheek and onion peel cells is the plant-versus-animal cell differentiation, named verbatim in LO-1. LO-8 also mentions these two slides, but it covers preparing and describing them, whereas the item asks for the contrast.
Cytoplasm as the jelly in which organelles float describes a microscopic feature. Not LO-1, because no comparison is made.
The Golgi apparatus as the packaging organelle describes a cell part by its function. Not LO-5, because no process is being explained step by step.
